checklist.detail: NARloy-Z Copper Alloy (Cu-Ag-Zr): computed wall temp 801 K EXCEEDS its 800 K max service temp (Tc 3428 K, regenerative cooling). Marginal/unsuitable as designed. Basis: coupled throat wall balance: gas h_g ~36.1 kW/m2K, T_aw ~3338 K, coolant ~155 m/s (coolant-side wall ~660 K), 0.50 mm wall. Levers that lower it: faster coolant (Coolant velocity; SP-8087 caps liquids at ~61 m/s, at a jacket-dP cost), a thinner wall, a liner rated hotter or more conductive (e.g. GRCop-84), or more film cooling.

checklist.detail: Hottest wall station is in the convergent section (area ratio ~1.0, regen): wall ~822 K, 0.97x that section's material limit (warns below 1.15x, like the throat row). Levers: more chamber film (or a convergent film ring for the throat region), faster coolant, a thinner or more conductive liner, or extend active cooling.

checklist.detail: Resultant injection beta angle +4.4 deg is outside the -4 to +2 deg band LOX/LH2 prefers - it wants a slightly negative beta (~0 or below). Adjust the impingement angle or element momentum ratio.
checklist.name: Injector resultant beta angle

checklist.detail: First tangential mode ~2876 Hz is in the band damaging instability lives in (<4000 Hz) and the injector is soft (dP/Pc 0.15 < 0.18). Historically this regime needed an odd-compartment injector-face baffle or corner-mounted Helmholtz cavities. Stiffen the injector, or plan on damping devices.
checklist.name: Combustion acoustic-mode margin

checklist.detail: Near the end of active cooling (area ratio ~45.0), estimated jacket/coolant pressure (~13.7 MPa) exceeds local hot-gas static pressure (~0.0 MPa) - the net load on the channel-land wall there REVERSES direction. Modeled as a clamped-strip bending stress across the ~16.0 mm channel width, this reversed ~13.7 MPa differential is ~7033 MPa against a ~133 MPa allowable (Inconel 718 Nickel Superalloy, SF 1.5) - but this is a coarse clamped-plate-strip proxy, NOT a real buckling/FEA analysis, and this codebase has no real-engine spot check for it yet. Treat this as 'worth a closer structural look', not a validated failure prediction. Consider more/narrower channels (smaller span), tapering the actively-cooled length, or a thicker wall there.
checklist.name: Jacket overpressure vs. channel-wall structural margin
